stories.topicLabel: Dolly Parton dies at age 80
stories.analysis: Coverage of Dolly Parton's death spanned a meaningful but moderate ideological range, with the clearest framing differences appearing in outlet-specific angles rather than in the basic death announcement itself. On the left end, the Los Angeles Times ran an appreciation emphasizing that Parton was "special to the LGBTQ+ community" and that "she showed us our country loves us," centering progressive community identity, while CNN layered in "humanitarian hero" and "queen" — laudatory, hagiographic language. Newsweek notably pivoted to partisan criticism, framing Parton's legacy through "Republicans Cut Funding for Dolly Parton's Child Reading Program." On the right, Breitbart highlighted a story about Parton "pulling gun from purse to stop NYC aggressor," a self-defense narrative with clear conservative audience appeal, while The Federalist celebrated "America's Best Love Song" in patriotic terms. The large middle of the coverage, however, was strikingly uniform — wire-style announcements describing a "music legend and philanthropist" with no detectable ideological charge.
